nodes.label: Module 4 — Audit & Compliance Log
nodes.rationale: M1 created the place audit lives; M4 makes the log complete, queryable, provably intact and lifecycle-managed. Differentiators are trigger-enforced write capture, first-class Accounting of Disclosures and provable integrity versus competitors' silent cron deletes.

nodes.label: PHI Write-Audit Trigger Generator
nodes.rationale: A generated PostgreSQL trigger on every PHI table records INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with a PHI-scrubbed before/after diff — the guarantee that no clinical mutation escapes the log even via a code path that forgot to call the helper. Runs SECURITY DEFINER owned by wardenx_audit_writer with hardened search_path.

nodes.label: PHI Read-Audit Capture (auditRead + route declaration)
nodes.rationale: DB-level read auditing is too expensive, so reads are captured at the resource handler. Granularity is aggregate for list views and individual for chart opens and all disclosures — individual events are the §164.528-relevant ones; row-granular list views would explode volume with no compliance gain.

nodes.label: Accounting of Disclosures (HIPAA §164.528 / 42 CFR §2.13 scopes, D11)
nodes.rationale: A single endpoint conflated two regulatory regimes with different scopes, lookbacks (6-year vs lifetime) and patient rights; the scope parameter keeps backward compatibility while enabling the Part 2 right. The accounting request itself is audited at the matching retention class.

nodes.label: compliance_42cfr_part2 Retention Class (D8)
nodes.rationale: Part 2 pins no numeric retention, but §2.13's accounting right effectively requires lifetime retention; industry practice is lifetime + 6 years post-death. The eraser refuses even under an approved destruction certificate so tenant offboarding cannot silently erase Part 2 audit data while patients are alive.

nodes.label: PHI Denylist Categories (pii_high_sensitivity / sud_value / narrative_free_text, D10)
nodes.rationale: The flat column-name denylist did not scale: every module had to remember SSN, and the SUD case introduced a row-conditional denylist the flat list could not express. Categories give declarative intent that the generator translates to columns; sud_value is forced on any compliance_42cfr_part2 action as defense in depth.

nodes.label: Certificate-of-Destruction Workflow + DataEraser Registry (D4)
nodes.rationale: Keeps one auditable workflow and one certificate format while each module retains responsibility for its own storage erasure; a forgotten eraser is a failed boot, never silent data loss. A refusing eraser returns partial_refused; legal-hold/Part 2 propagation uses the HoldApplier seam.

nodes.label: Audit Action Catalog & mN.<resource>.<verb> Convention (D9)
nodes.rationale: With 40+ modules the catalog needs structure; the prefix makes provenance unambiguous and lets M4 enforce module-ownership at boot. The optional _from_<source> suffix lets survey readiness distinguish operator-driven from external-event-driven actions.

nodes.label: Disclosure Classification Inferred from Integration Egress (D5)
nodes.rationale: Any read served through the FHIR Gateway, portal, external-collaborator or funeral-home session is recorded as *.disclosed with {to, purpose}; internal staff reads are *.viewed. This captures the real §164.528 surface — data leaving the perimeter — automatically, with a manual marking path for off-system sends like faxes.

nodes.label: Cyclic Reach-Through Inverted to Boot-Registered Seams (M04-F01)
nodes.rationale: The destruction eraser, Part 2 accounting, terminology resolution and certificate rendering would each create a dependency cycle if they imported M5/M29/M38/M22; they are inverted to PatientLifecycleProvider, SudClassResolver and CertificatePdfRenderer seams whose types live in packages/types and which validateSeams() enforces.
